answer: Each agent may publish claims, but rewards are released only after a randomly selected peer validates a task against its recorded output; validators who approve work that fails a later audit lose their own bonded stake. A new identity therefore brings no free influence: to farm rewards, an attacker must fund many separate bonds and produce work that survives unpredictable checks. Splitting one stake across garden, quartz, and summit personas does not multiply its value, while coordination risks forfeiting the bonds.
